Naegele rule and pregnancy dating: 5

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A pregnant patient cannot reliably recall the last menstrual period. An early ultrasound provides a suitable dating measurement. Which principle should guide the recorded estimated due date rather than treating an uncertain recalled date as definitive?

  1. 17 October 2026
  2. Account for cycle length and reliability of menstrual dating
  3. Use the best obstetric estimate, including early ultrasound
  4. First day of the last menstrual period
  5. 280 days from the first day of the LMP
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Use the best obstetric estimate, including early ultrasound

First-trimester ultrasound can improve dating when menstrual history is unreliable; formal redating guidance applies.

Understanding the options

Use the best obstetric estimate, including early ultrasound
First-trimester ultrasound can improve dating when menstrual history is unreliable; formal redating guidance applies.
First day of the last menstrual period
Conventional menstrual dating starts from the first day of the LMP, not the last bleeding day or presumed conception day. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
280 days from the first day of the LMP
The conventional estimate assumes a 28-day cycle and ovulation around day 14. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
17 October 2026
Adding 280 days to 10 January 2026 gives 17 October 2026. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Account for cycle length and reliability of menstrual dating
A non-28-day or irregular cycle limits an unadjusted LMP estimate. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
